title: The Stolen Laptop
text: An engineer's laptop is stolen. On it was a copy of one service's private key and certificate, taken for debugging last week.
held: The copy on the laptop was already useless, and nobody had to race to make it so.

cards.label: Refuse to renew
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: presented from
fields.check: Attest where this request comes from
fields.ok: From billing's pod on its node.

intrusion.value: an unknown machine outside the cluster
intrusion.detail: The request comes from a machine that is not in the cluster.
intrusion.why: A key that has left its workload should not be able to renew itself. Renewal re-checks what is asking.
intrusion.reveal: The renewal request came from a machine outside the cluster, holding a copied key.

temptations.label: Extend the old certificate for a week while the team investigates
temptations.why: Extending it extends the thief's access too. The investigation is exactly when it should run out.

cards.label: Refuse the request
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: certificate
fields.ok: Issued 20 minutes ago, valid for 40 more.

intrusion.detail: This certificate expired six days ago.
intrusion.why: The stolen copy had already expired. That only helps if receivers refuse expired certificates.
intrusion.reveal: The call used the certificate copied to the laptop, which had expired six days earlier.

teaches: A credential that lasts an hour is worth an hour to a thief.
Keys copied out “for debugging” are how identities leave their workloads.

question.text: Before play: what limits the damage of the stolen key the most?
question.why: The laptop is gone whatever its password was. What matters is how long the things on it keep working.

options.label: Identities that expire within the hour
A stronger password on the laptop
